reviews.title: How long are we gonna put up with this?
reviews.text:
First off, the pricing model is totally predatory. The only free trial is if you agree to be charged a whole year’s membership fee after the seven-day trial period.  There’s no free trial if you opt for just monthly payments. I wonder why that would be?  Also, how long are we going to tolerate apps asking you a bunch of irrelevant questions prior to even being able to test the app?  Can I please just test your service without feeling like I’m being herded?   

When I finally got to the app, I realized it was overly complicated and could not really do what I wanted it to do, which was track the amount of time I spend in specific habits by using timers for those activities.  Overall, I feel like I was charged $13 so that I could make the 30 second assessment that this app was not for me. This could have been avoided with a free trial.

reviews.title: Loved this app until the latest update.
reviews.text: Prior to the latest update I absolutely loved the app. I was a free user, and even then it did exactly what I wanted it to: set pomodoro seshes, track my time among different tasks—it was perfect. The option to block apps was there (though I personally never used it). Now, the app forces app blockage, and the only way to really get rid of it is to manually block screen time access in settings, which we shouldn’t have to do in the first place. We shouldn’t have to PAY to turn off a feature that we were previously able to toggle ourselves. I agree with many recent reviews in that this 100% feels like a money grabbing update. Most of all, I dislike the inability to pause automatically timers whenever a focus or break session is done. Instead, it automatically goes into the next break or focus session. Though for some they prefer this feature, me personally it makes me lose track of what focus session I’m on. A pause  allows me to better keep track of it, and the fact that this is no longer a feature is driving me away from this app.

reviews.title: Elegance and functionality declining with every new update
reviews.text: This was a 5 star app and now it’s a 2 or 3 star. The original reason I chose this app many years ago is because it had the simplest, elegant design while also offering key features like easy customization of the short and long break timing, number of sessions, notifications, ability to pause and restart. Then came the updates and gamification, trying to be something that it never will be: a task management app? From someone with lifelong ADHD, it’s disappointing that you’re jumping on the more is better bandwagon. More is more confusing and clunky and honestly very cheesy if not implemented well. I’m looking for a sleek tool for the toolbox not a new toolbox. Many new updates in this app interrupts core functionality and usability and often causes more distraction and less focus. Have you tested the UX of this app thoroughly? Have user groups weighed in? I just begrudgingly opened for the first time in a while and now I can’t find any way to set the number of sessions. Months ago wasn’t much better—while you still could adjust the break options, there were two different ways to do it (global and task specific) and neither worked well. I usually had to restart for the timer to adjust. I have zero issue paying a reasonable fee for a good app. But that’s only if it’s going to thoughtful design.
